sections.title: The Wedding at Cana
observations: This passage describes Jesus' first miracle, turning water into wine at a wedding in Cana. It highlights the significance of Jesus' presence at social events and His willingness to engage in human celebrations.
The act of turning water into wine symbolizes the transformation that Jesus brings into the lives of believers. It also reflects the abundance and joy of the Kingdom of God.

sections.title: Cleansing the Temple
observations: In this section, Jesus cleanses the temple, driving out the money changers and those selling animals for sacrifice. This act demonstrates His authority over the temple and His zeal for true worship.

Jesus' actions challenge the commercialization of religion and emphasize the importance of reverence in worship. His statement about the temple being His Father's house underscores His divine identity.

sections.title: The Response of the People
observations: After the cleansing of the temple, the Jews demand a sign to validate Jesus' authority. Jesus responds by speaking of the destruction of the temple and His resurrection, which they misunderstand.
This interaction reveals the spiritual blindness of the religious leaders and foreshadows the conflict that will arise between Jesus and the Jewish authorities.

importantVerses.commentary: This verse highlights the significance of Jesus' first miracle, revealing His glory and leading His disciples to believe in Him.
Jesus' declaration about destroying the temple and raising it in three days points to His resurrection and the new covenant.

questions: What does the miracle at Cana reveal about Jesus' character and mission?
How does the cleansing of the temple reflect Jesus' view of worship and the church?
In what ways do the responses of the people demonstrate their understanding (or misunderstanding) of Jesus' identity?
